page: Microsoft Azure D16alds_v7 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the Daldsv7 family. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical AMD EPYC 9V45 cores running at 4.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 2.0 GB per core ratio. Local storage is provided via a 945 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance is premium storage capable, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU, Geekbench single-core, and single-threaded gzip and bzip3 operations ranking in the top 10%. Multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core, falls into the average category. Memory bandwidth and database operations also perform at average levels, while text generation for small LLM models achieves top-tier throughput.

With a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this server represents a resource-dense compute option. It offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring high clock speeds and fast local NVMe storage without the overhead of excess memory. However, the 32.0 GB memory capacity presents a tradeoff for memory-intensive applications, which may experience bottlenecks.

This configuration fits single-threaded tasks, web serving, software compilation, and lightweight LLM text generation. The combination of a 4.5 GHz CPU and local NVMe SSD makes it appropriate for database operations and compute-bound workloads with moderate memory requirements.
